text:
andrea: scanner flagged CVE-2026-9999 in our base image (openssl RCE). severity=CRITICAL. we should coordinate an image rebuild + signing plan. do we halt new canaries?

samir: paste the exact image tag + scanner snippet plz. need to know if this lives in an upstream distro layer or our build.

andrea: image: `gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-03-18`
scanner excerpt:
```
VULN CVE-2026-9999 | package: openssl | version: 3.0.6 | CVSS: 9.8
affected file: /usr/lib/libssl.so.1.1
layer: sha256:abcd...ef12
```

maria: even if it's upstream, we should rebuild so we control the final artifact (strip debug, remove unnecessary tools). Also we need extended audit retention around signing events for the incident window. tagging compliance.

security-oncall: do NOT revoke or rotate signing key versions yet. quick play: 1) pause new canaries, 2) create patched base in staging, 3) run attestations and smoke tests, 4) cosign-sign with current active key version, 5) small canary rollout + observe, 6) full rollout, 7) rotate keys only after all old images are out of prod and verification windows closed.

leo: question about KMS envelopes — our key resource is `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/image/cryptoKeys/signer-v2`. If we create new keyversion and make it primary, will signatures made with prior versions still validate?

security-oncall: verification checks the public key for the version embedded in the signature. as long as we don't disable the old key version, verification succeeds. so keep old versions enabled until cleanup. recommended: do not disable for at least 14 days; target 30 days. communicate in #release-war-room prior to disable.

devops-bot: scan-alert -> gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-03-18 -> CVE-2026-9999 -> ticket INC-789 created (P0).

andrea: proposed immediate checklist:
- freeze new canaries (ci: block canary job)
- produce patched base image: apply distro patches, run `strip --strip-all` on binaries, remove pkg manager
- rebuild in staging, run smoke + perf (startup, kv cache behaviour)
- run cosign sign + attestation using current signer key version
- canary rollout 2% for 30m; watch for cosign verification errors, startup failures, latency regressions
- if green, ramp to 100%
volunteers for monitoring the canary window?

samir: i'll own canary monitoring. opening IAM MR to allow CI-SA temporary signer permission. MR: `https://gitlab.com/redwood/infra/merge_requests/321` — binding snippet:
```
resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "ci-keystore" {
  role = "roles/keystore.signer"
  members = ["serviceAccount:ci-pipeline@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
```

maria: I'll file the SIEM retention PR to extend image-sign and KMS usage logs from 30d -> 180d for `org:redwood-prod`. ETA ~1h. tagging compliance and legal.

security-oncall: assigning owners: andrea (build), samir (canary+IAM), maria (audit retention). I'll watch and coordinate with infra oncall. If any cosign verification errors or KMS access denials show up, escalate immediately.

leo: follow-on: what's our safe revoke timeline/policy once images are rotated? we should document it in the incident note.

security-oncall: policy draft: do not revoke key versions until 14 days after last production deployment signed with that version; prefer 30 days to cover staggered rollouts and cross-region delays. post a revoke intention 48h beforehand in #release-war-room.

andrea: starting staging build now. will post build id and cosign log when ready. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: build: staging/base:2026-03-18-patched #4521 started.

maria: SIEM ticket filed: SIEM-1245, linked to INC-789. PR for retention change created and assigned to infra-seq.

security-oncall: keeping this thread open. if anything blocks signing (KMS permission issues, cosign failures), ping me and infra-oncall.

(andrea later): staging build finished, cosign attest succeeded. canary scheduled at 14:30 UTC for 2% traffic. samir taking watch.
